A.reason: Candidate 6 provides a feasible accessible first-come queue with explicit two-attendant roles, protected emergency access, place preservation, safe interruption recovery and tracking across both events, including unfinished waits. Candidates 6 and 7 refine existing mechanisms rather than introduce new ones. Candidate 5 is usable only if its stated turnover or enforceable-duration prerequisite is established; it explicitly prohibits operation otherwise. Other conditional approaches also require their stated site prerequisites.

B.reason: Candidate 0 offers the simplest workable allocation rule, accessible waiting accommodations, clear attendant roles and measurement of all required outcomes across two events. Its main limitation is uncontrolled visit duration. Cohorts could improve turnover but require safe, authorized session enforcement; priority shares and draws add administration without an established advantage. No candidate definitely violates a hard constraint.

pair.reason: A6 improves on B0's shared first-come mechanism with concrete stop-and-resume rules, explicit protection of recorded accessible places, occupancy reconciliation and an end-of-hour procedure. These address practical risks within the two-attendant limit, while its evaluation includes unresolved waits and appropriately limits claims about unobserved interruptions.
